THE SAGGING BRASS SHELF: a long timber shelf bowing along the wall's curve, five turned brass cylinders standing on end, a coil of brass wire looped beside them, one small brass cup welded to the shelf in its own puddle of old wax.

THE SHELF WITH THE HAND CRANK: a curved timber shelf carrying three brass cylinders leaning together, a little brass bell on its side, and a hand crank off its machine lying where it was set down, brass worn bright at the grip.

THE SHELF OF SMALL BRASS CUPS: seven small brass cups stacked one on another along the curved shelf, the top cup tilted, a coil of brass wire draped over the stack's far side, one cup brimming with cold candle wax.

THE CROWDED LOWER SHELF: a thick timber shelf sagging heavily at one end along the wall's curve, carrying a hand crank, three brass cylinders on end, and a brass bell hung by a loop of cord over a rough iron nail in the beam above.

THE BANK OF PAINTED DRAWERS: a tall bank of small timber drawers built against the curve, fronts grouped in flat bands of ochre, rust and deep blue, each with one turned bone knob, one drawer standing a finger's width open.

THE DRAWER WITH THE ACORN KNOB: a tall bank of small timber drawers following the wall's curve, fronts painted in stepped bands of amber and grey, one knob replaced with a carved wooden acorn, one drawer open showing pale pebbles inside.

THE BLUE GROUP OF DRAWERS: a bank of small timber drawers, the top seven painted deep blue and the lower nine painted brick red, each with a bone knob, one of the blue drawers standing open with three pale river pebbles sitting in it.

THE DRAWER BANK BY THE BEAM: a curved bank of small timber drawers, fronts in flat bands of moss green and cream, bone knobs slightly uneven in height, the lowest drawer on the left pulled half open and resting on the floorboard below it.

THE RING MACHINE ON ITS STAND: nested brass rings one inside another on a turned wooden stand, small painted balls riding the rings, the outermost ring leaning a little left, the whole thing about as wide across as two floorboards.

THE HEAVY BRASS DISC: nested brass rings on a turned wooden stand beside a heavy brass disc hung on a looped chain from a beam, the disc swinging slightly, and a squat iron weight sitting on the boards beneath it, flat-topped and dark.

THE RING MACHINE AND THE WEIGHT: nested brass rings on a turned wooden stand, five small painted balls at uneven positions along them, and a squat iron weight beside it on the boards, its flat top worn to a lighter grey where hands have lifted it.

THE BRASS DISC BY THE WINDOW BOARDS: a heavy brass disc hung on a chain dropping from the roof beam, turning slowly, and a squat iron weight on the floor below, and a turned wooden stand beside them holding nested brass rings, the smallest ring tilted.

THE ROLLING LADDER WITH THE LAMP: the rolling ladder leaning against the wall's curve, an oil lamp on a hook at its third rung, a coil of rope draped over a lower rung, a single boot standing on the floor at the ladder's foot.

THE LADDER WITH THE LONG COAT: the rolling ladder standing against the curve, a long coat and a striped scarf hung over the top rung, one sleeve trailing, a coil of rope over a middle rung, an oil lamp hooked beside it.

THE LADDER WITH THE MITTENS: the rolling ladder leaning at the curve, a pair of mittens spread over the third rung to dry, a rope's end dangling from the fourth rung bound with a bright thread of red, an oil lamp hooked at the side.

THE LADDER AT THE CURVE: the rolling ladder standing against the wall's curve, a long coat on the top rung, a coil of rope looped over a lower one, a pair of mittens stuffed into the coat's left pocket, an oil lamp hanging alongside.

THE CAT BY THE BRAZIER: one cat asleep curled on the warm boards beside the low brazier, no longer than two floorboards are wide, tail curved over its nose, a small dish of milk gone cold on the boards beside it.

THE OWL ON THE RIB: one barn owl standing on a dome rib with its back to the room, about as tall as the brass bell on the shelf below, feathers flat, the rib casting a hard pixel-stepped shadow across the plaster behind it.

THE MOTH AT THE LAMP: one pale moth going round and round the oil lamp on the bracket, no wider than a thumb across its wings, casting a soft flickering shadow that sweeps the curved plaster wall with each slow pass.

THE DOG BY THE STOVE: one small rough-coated dog asleep against the iron stove, about as long as one floorboard is wide, one ear folded up and one ear down, a feather blown from somewhere stuck upright in a crack in the boards beside its nose.

THE LOW WORKING TABLE: a low timber table carrying a candle stub burnt down into its own wax puddle in a saucer, a tin cup, a wide shallow bowl of still water catching the lamplight, a cup ring worn dark into the wood beside the bowl.

THE LOW WORKING TABLE: a low timber table with a tin cup, a saucer of spare pins with one pin standing much higher than the rest, a wide shallow bowl of still water, and a candle stub burnt right down into its own puddle of wax.

THE TABLE WITH THE PINS: a low timber table carrying a candle stub in a saucer, a wide shallow bowl of still water, a saucer of five spare pins with one pin standing at a tilt, and a broom leaning in the curve of the wall behind it.

THE FLOOR BY THE STOVE: a stack of split firewood on the boards beside the iron stove, seven logs with one set apart and standing on its end, a tin cup left on the stove top, a broom leaning in the curve, its bristles worn down on one side.

THE BARREL IN THE CORNER: a barrel standing in the curve of the wall holding three rolled hides tied with cord, the hides different heights, one hide's cord knotted twice, a broom leaning against the barrel. a single worn boot standing beside it on the boards.
